text:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated CUDA OOM rate on cluster serving-west-1 (nodeset: shared-hosted). Rule: runtime.cuda_oom_rate > 1/min for 5m. Link: https://infra.redwood/alert/1777654321 :rotating_light:

nina_p: noticed errors around 09:03 UTC. Observed gradual rise in GPU memory until OOMs then container restarts. no recent deploys to the affected service.

omar_h: quick grep of logs shows repeated: 
```
2026-03-02T09:04:11Z runtime WARN: attention_pager: slab_drain_attempts=3 reclaimed=0
2026-03-02T09:04:11Z runtime ERROR: cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-02T09:04:12Z kubelet: container exited with code 137 (OOMKilled)
```

ton y_g: (typo oops) tony_g: looks like slab "drip" where small free ranges accumulate and bitmap scan misses them. we saw this pattern in lab but slower. slab fragmentation + sticky KV prefixes holding refs.

sasha_m: customer-ops ping: two customers reported spikes of 503/504 and increased 99th latency. both on shared pool. dedicated customers unaffected.

nina_p: initial mitigation plan: 1) throttle prefix cache TTL for heavy endpoints; 2) bump allocator eviction multiplier to 0.9 on one node; 3) schedule targeted slab compaction one node at a time; 4) avoid cluster-wide runtime restarts.

oncall: please follow runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/slab-drip. capture outputs in incident doc and don't parallelize compaction on more than 2 nodes.

infa ra-bot: autoprobe results: node-5 slab_frag=0.71 mem_growth=5.8%/hr, node-8 slab_frag=0.64 mem_growth=3.2%/hr, node-11 slab_frag=0.35 mem_growth=0.8%/hr.

omar_h: starting with node-5 (worst offender). cordon + drain then run compaction. commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon node-5
kubectl drain node-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh node-5 'sudo /opt/redwood/bin/slab-compact --run --aggressive=1'
```

nina_p: running the compact now on node-5 (09:18). estimate ~40s. will monitor OOMs.

infra-bot: compaction job started: job-compact-1777 on node-5. logs: https://infra.redwood/logs/job-compact-1777

omar_h: compaction output:
```
compact: before_frag=0.71 after_frag=0.33 reclaimed=38% time=52s cpu_spike=2x
```

tony_g: reclaimed 38% is solid. starting eviction multiplier increase on node-8 to 0.9 (live change):
```bash
curl -s -X POST http://node-8:8080/admin/allocator -d '{"evict_mult":0.9}'
```

sasha_m: node-8 did a graceful adjust. observed immediate small drop in resident GPU memory (~3%). OOMs on cluster dropped to 0 events/min for 12m.

nina_p: also temporarily reduced prefix-cache TTL for route /v1/chat to 20s for heavy tenants via config rollout (canary then roll): applied to canary subset (~3 pods).

customer-ops: customer update draft: "We detected elevated memory pressure causing intermittent errors and high tail latency for a small set of shared-hosted customers. Engineers applied targeted memory compaction and eviction tuning; most requests recovered and we are continuing to monitor. No customer data was affected." :white_check_mark:

omar_h: observed one noisy node (node-12) still creeping. plan: restart paged-attn helper on node-12 (non-disruptive) then run a non-blocking slab recheck. command: `systemctl restart redwood-paged-helper`

infra-bot: helper restart on node-12 completed; helper logs show incremental freed_refs=412 after restart.

nina_p: after these mitigations: cluster OOMs reduced from ~6/min to ~0.2/min. tail latency subsided. continuing to monitor for 1h.

oncall: decision: don't roll global hotfix yet. proceed node-by-node compaction + eviction tweaks. lower per-container GPU limit? pros: prevents OOM cascade, cons: may increase throttling. suggestions?

tony_g: propose reduce per-container mem cap by 8% on canary pods for 30m, measure error rate. I'll prepare patch: kube resource limit -> container.env REDWOOD_GPU_SOFT_LIMIT=0.92

omar_h: +1 from me. prepare rollback plan: if error rate > 1% in canary, revert.

sasha_m: acknowledged. will watch customer impact and route traffic away if we see regressions.

nina_p: filing interim ticket for post-incident: INF-2099 "allocator: background defrag worker + improved scan heuristics" assigned to eng-runtime. include small benchmark reproducer.

customer-ops: sent status update to affected tenants at 09:50 UTC. they asked for ETA; we'll follow up after stable period (30m).

nina_p: final note: observed one runtime container crash with CUBLAS kernel panic on node-5 during compaction window. investigating with logs attached (link: https://infra.redwood/logs/crash-1777). likely unrelated but opened INF-2100 for follow-up.

oncall: handing off to night oncall (sasha_m) at 23:00 UTC. tasks left: monitor OOM rate, keep eviction multiplier tweak on nodes with frag >0.5, do not compact >2 nodes in parallel, and update INF-2099 with any reproducer notes.

sasha_m: take it. will escalate to eng-runtime if OOM rate rises above 2/min or if more than 2 nodes show frag >0.6.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations in place; severity set to P3. auto-close after 12h stability.
